description: Coordinator hooks — session guardrails and cost optimization. REGISTRATIONS IN THIS FILE ARE READ AT SESSION START AND CACHED: adding or removing an entry here reaches NO already-running session until it runs /reload-plugins or restarts, and a deleted entry keeps firing until then. Run /reload-plugins in this session before testing your change, and expect peer sessions on this machine to keep their booted roster regardless. Hook SCRIPT bodies are unaffected — those resolve live per tool call. Measurement: docs/wiki/external-plugin-live-resolution.md § Hook REGISTRATION staleness; tripwire HOOKS-JSON-REGISTRATION-STALENESS.

SessionStart._comment: foreign-platform-path guard (claude-klabauter session.guard_foreign_platform_paths op, called in-process). 2026-07-28 incident: a POSIX host's settings.json silently rewritten with Windows drive-letter hook-command paths (DoE-claude/...) by a sync/commit race on the ~/.claude meta-repo -- every one of ~40 hooks died with NO error anywhere, only tool calls failing against a drive that does not exist here. Detect-only (never auto-repairs -- settings.json is shared with another machine via git sync; a same-host repair could clobber the OTHER machine's next pull), shape-based (regex, never a hardcoded drive letter/username), banner-only, fail-open at every uncertain step, sync (its output is additionalContext the model needs to see). Delivery, re-verified 2026-07-28 on a POSIX host (this comment previously asserted the opposite and was stale): plugin-declared hooks in THIS file DO deliver via --plugin-dir. Live proof -- ~/.claude/settings.json carried an EMPTY hooks block (zero commands; settings.json was untracked in the meta-repo as machine-local) while pickup-autofire.py, registered nowhere but this file, fired normally. Do not re-derive the 'hook-delivery is dead, bug #38699' premise from the wiki without re-probing it; a sibling repo generalized a dead plugin hook of its own into 'plugin hooks.json never delivers', and that generalization does not hold here -- their dead hook loads via a directory-source marketplace, a different delivery mechanism. Residual gap that remains real regardless: an EXTERNAL rewrite (git sync, another machine's push) is not a tool call and lands between sessions, so no PreToolUse guard sees it and a SessionStart guard only reports it after the fact. The independent second leg for that is the native git pre-commit hook coordinator-precommit-foreign-platform-check (claude-klabauter), which fires via git itself on the WRITING machine and survives a session where every Claude Code hook is dead. The mid-session tool-write leg is guard-settings-json-write.py, registered below.

SessionStart._comment: C1b — asserts EM identity to the main session via snippets/agent-role-em.md. Deliberately a SEPARATE hook from the orientation injector above, not a fold-in: orientation is staleness-nudged and suppressible (COORDINATOR_REPOMAP_STATUS_OFF et al., quiet degrade on a missing cache); a role assertion sharing that suppressibility would be worse than none. Relies on SessionStart-class hooks firing only for the main session, never an Agent-tool dispatch -- no additional is-main-session guard is layered on top here. The matcher must enumerate EVERY SessionStart source, not just cold start: the harness emits startup, resume, clear, compact and fork, and an omitted source means the hook simply does not fire for it. A startup|clear|compact matcher silently loses the role assertion on --resume/--continue and on --fork-session, which are precisely the long-lived sessions where the EM has most drifted from its role. This hook's contract is unconditional delivery, so its matcher is exhaustive by construction rather than mirroring any sibling hook's narrower coverage.

SessionEnd._comment: Best-effort archival of this session's coordinator-sessions bookkeeping dir (nudge sentinels, dispatch evidence, started_at, meta.json), moved HERE from the /workstream-complete ceremony because that ceremony fires mid-session -- a session can close several workstreams before it actually ends, and archiving there reset once-per-session guards a still-live session still needed. SessionEnd fires exactly once, when the session is genuinely over. Matcher '' fires on every SessionEnd reason (clear, logout, prompt_input_exit, other) -- archival is wanted regardless of why the session ended. Shells out to the claude-klabauter-resident coordinator/bin/wsc-close.py archive-session --sid <sid> CLI (already non-fatal-by-design; see that script's own module docstring) rather than importing coordinator_core.session.scope directly, so this repo has exactly one thin caller of an entrypoint claude-klabauter already built for this call. Fails silently in every direction (unparsable stdin, absent session_id, unresolvable claude-klabauter root, subprocess timeout/failure) -- the 24h reaper is the documented backstop, so this hook must never block session teardown. Never falls back to a pid-derived or guessed session key.

Emits nothing (DEC-4: a SubagentStop hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext reaches only the subagent's own context, never the EM's -- Stage 2, folded into the existing UserPromptSubmit runtime-tripwire-em-check.py entry below, is what surfaces it). Registered LAST, only after the claude-klabauter op landed (claude-klabauter commit 82224422) -- an unregistered script is inert; a registered one that silently no-ops on every SubagentStop until the op exists is the exact fail-open-reads-as-healthy shape this workstream exists to kill. This registration percolates to every OSS install of the coordinator plugin, most of which have no claude-klabauter and therefore no engine op to resolve -- for those installs this is a permanent per-SubagentStop python3 cold start (~642ms on the reference Windows machine) that can only ever no-op, same as the other _engine_root-gated entries in this file; precedented, not a blocker, but named here rather than shipped silently.

UserPromptExpansion._comment: mise-en-place run-id auto-mint (the mise-side twin of the pickup-autofire entry above). Fires ahead of UserPromptSubmit on a `mise-en-place` verb invocation; the script matches command_name (same bare-verb-vs-namespaced normalization as pickup-autofire.py), mints a fresh Phase-0 run id through the engine plane's `backlog-grind-assemble mint-run-id mise-en-place` CLI, immediately briefs that same id back through `backlog-grind-assemble brief mise-en-place --run-id <minted>`, and injects the minted id, its implied (not-yet-existing) inventory path, and the brief's decision object as additionalContext. Both calls are read-only -- this hook has no mutating apply-equivalent and must never grow one; Phase 6 stays an EM-driven invocation quoting the minted id. Never creates state/mise-inventory/ itself: that directory's absence is the engine's own Phase-0-vs-Phase-6 self-gate (see the script's own module docstring). async:false because the minted id must land in the SAME turn the EM's prompt is being expanded into. Every failure mode (unresolvable CLI, non-zero exit, timeout, malformed JSON, missing keys) degrades to silent pass -- this hook never blocks /mise-en-place; a failed mint just means the EM mints by hand, today's behaviour. Provenance: engine-plane commit 339470fd6bd7 shipped the mint-run-id verb; cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-04-claude-klabauter-em-mint-run-id-verb-shipped.md pins the consumer contract this hook relies on.

PreToolUse._comment: BLOCK-WORKTREE-TOOL — structural git-worktree ban, one leg of a multi-leg campaign. Denies EnterWorktree unconditionally (worktrees degrade on Windows and don't scale to concurrent-agent dispatch; the sanctioned shape is scoped-parallel dispatch into the same tree). ExitWorktree always ALLOWED — leaving a worktree is cleanup, never blocked, or an agent already inside one gets trapped. Override: repo-root sentinel file ONLY (no env-var leg — a subagent can set an env var on itself, defeating an env-var override for a guard that must bind subagents too). Deny message deliberately never names the sentinel file.

Each guard writes its own advisory directly to stderr and returns exit 2 (the Stop-family protocol, distinct from the PreToolUse deny/additionalContext envelope shape `preuse-write-dispatch.py` uses); this dispatcher batches all four into ONE process via the in-process Stop-family runner (coordinator/hooks/scripts/_stop_family_runner.py), aggregating via CONCATENATE-ALL (never first-fires-wins — every guard that fires on a payload has its text reach the combined stderr, and the combined exit code is 2 if any fired). See coordinator/hooks/scripts/_stop_family_runner_contract.py for why this is a SIBLING mechanism to _guard_runner.py, not an extension of it. Policy byte-identical — this moves WHERE these guards run, never what they decide.
